---
title: "Low-Level Offboard Control"
---

Low-level offboard control means bypassing PX4's position/velocity controllers
and sending commands directly to the inner loops. Three levels are available,
selected at runtime via a ROS 2 parameter:

| Mode | `control_mode` | PX4 message | What you command |
|------|:--------------:|-------------|-----------------|
| Attitude | 1 | `VehicleAttitudeSetpoint` | Desired quaternion + collective thrust |
| Thrust + Torque | 2 | `VehicleThrustSetpoint` + `VehicleTorqueSetpoint` | Body-frame wrench |
| Direct actuator | 3 | `ActuatorMotors` | Per-motor throttle [0, 1] |

Reference implementation:
[SaxionMechatronics/px4_offboard_lowlevel](https://github.com/SaxionMechatronics/px4_offboard_lowlevel).

---

## OffboardControlMode heartbeat

PX4 requires a continuous `OffboardControlMode` heartbeat at ~3 Hz or it
exits offboard mode. The active fields must match the command type being sent:

```cpp
px4_msgs::msg::OffboardControlMode msg{};
msg.position          = false;
msg.velocity          = false;
msg.acceleration      = false;
msg.body_rate         = false;

// mode 1 — attitude
msg.attitude          = true;
msg.thrust_and_torque = false;
msg.direct_actuator   = false;

// mode 2 — thrust + torque
// msg.thrust_and_torque = true; (attitude and direct_actuator = false)

// mode 3 — direct actuator
// msg.direct_actuator = true; (attitude and thrust_and_torque = false)

msg.timestamp = node->get_clock()->now().nanoseconds() / 1000;
offboard_control_mode_pub->publish(msg);
```

The heartbeat timer and the controller output timer are independent:

```cpp
// 3 Hz heartbeat
offboard_timer = create_wall_timer(333ms, [=]() { publishOffboardControlModeMsg(); });

// 100 Hz control loop
controller_timer = create_wall_timer(10ms,  [=]() { updateControllerOutput(); });
```

---

## Frame conventions

PX4 uses **NED / FRD** (North-East-Down, Front-Right-Down). ROS and most
controllers use **ENU / FLU** (East-North-Up, Front-Left-Up). All setpoints
must be converted before publishing, and all odometry must be converted after
reading.

See [Frame Conventions](frame-conventions.qmd) for the full conversion
reference including vector permutations, quaternion transforms, altitude sign,
and yaw convention.

---

## Mode 1: Attitude setpoint

Publish `VehicleAttitudeSetpoint` with a desired quaternion and collective
thrust. The PX4 attitude controller tracks the quaternion error.

```cpp
px4_msgs::msg::VehicleAttitudeSetpoint msg{};
msg.timestamp = node->get_clock()->now().nanoseconds() / 1000;

Eigen::Quaterniond q_ned = rotateQuaternionFromToENU_NED(desired_q);
msg.q_d[0] = q_ned.w();
msg.q_d[1] = q_ned.x();
msg.q_d[2] = q_ned.y();
msg.q_d[3] = q_ned.z();

msg.thrust_body[0] = 0.0;
msg.thrust_body[1] = 0.0;
msg.thrust_body[2] = -collective_thrust;   // NED: downward = negative

attitude_setpoint_pub->publish(msg);
```

---

## Mode 2: Thrust + torque setpoint

Publish separate `VehicleThrustSetpoint` and `VehicleTorqueSetpoint` messages.
PX4 uses these directly — no attitude controller in the loop.

```cpp
px4_msgs::msg::VehicleThrustSetpoint thrust_msg{};
px4_msgs::msg::VehicleTorqueSetpoint torque_msg{};

uint64_t ts = node->get_clock()->now().nanoseconds() / 1000;
thrust_msg.timestamp = thrust_msg.timestamp_sample = ts;
torque_msg.timestamp = torque_msg.timestamp_sample = ts;

thrust_msg.xyz[0] = 0.0;
thrust_msg.xyz[1] = 0.0;
thrust_msg.xyz[2] = -collective_thrust;   // NED sign

// Rotate torque from controller FLU frame to FRD
Eigen::Vector3d tau_frd = rotateVectorFromToFRD_FLU(torque_flu);
torque_msg.xyz[0] = tau_frd.x();
torque_msg.xyz[1] = tau_frd.y();
torque_msg.xyz[2] = tau_frd.z();

thrust_pub->publish(thrust_msg);
torque_pub->publish(torque_msg);
```

---

## Mode 3: Direct actuator commands

Publish `ActuatorMotors` with per-motor throttles in [0, 1]. Unused slots
must be `NaN`.

```cpp
px4_msgs::msg::ActuatorMotors msg{};
msg.control = {
    (float) throttles[0], (float) throttles[1],
    (float) throttles[2], (float) throttles[3],
    std::nanf("1"), std::nanf("1"), std::nanf("1"), std::nanf("1"),
    std::nanf("1"), std::nanf("1"), std::nanf("1"), std::nanf("1")
};
msg.reversible_flags = 0;
msg.timestamp = msg.timestamp_sample = node->get_clock()->now().nanoseconds() / 1000;
actuator_motors_pub->publish(msg);
```

::: {.callout-warning}
**Lockstep must be disabled** for direct actuator control in Gazebo SITL.
Set `lockstep: false` in the model's `model.sdf` and in PX4's SITL config.
:::

---

## Control allocation (wrench -> throttles)

To produce per-motor throttles from a desired wrench `[tau_x, tau_y, tau_z, T]`:

$$
\boldsymbol{\omega} = \mathbf{M}^+ \mathbf{w}, \quad
\text{PWM}_i = c_2 \omega_i^2 + c_1 \omega_i + c_0, \quad
\delta_i = \frac{\text{PWM}_i - \text{PWM}_\text{min}}{\text{PWM}_\text{max} - \text{PWM}_\text{min}}
$$

where $\mathbf{M}$ is the control allocation matrix (arm geometry + motor
constants) and $\mathbf{M}^+$ is its pseudoinverse.

For a symmetric X-quadrotor with arm length $l$ and thrust/moment constants
$k_T$, $k_M$:

$$
\mathbf{M} = \begin{pmatrix}
-k_T l \sin 45^\circ & k_T l \sin 45^\circ & k_T l \sin 45^\circ & -k_T l \sin 45^\circ \\
-k_T l \sin 45^\circ & k_T l \sin 45^\circ & -k_T l \sin 45^\circ & k_T l \sin 45^\circ \\
-k_M k_T & -k_M k_T & k_M k_T & k_M k_T \\
k_T & k_T & k_T & k_T
\end{pmatrix}
$$

SITL skips the PWM conversion and maps throttles directly via `SIM_GZ_EC_MIN`
/ `SIM_GZ_EC_MAX` (rotor speed limits in rad/s).

### x500 parameters (reference)

```yaml
uav_parameters:
  mass: 2.064              # kg
  arm_length: 0.25         # m
  num_of_arms: 4
  inertia: {x: 0.08612, y: 0.08962, z: 0.16088}   # kg.m^2
  thrust_constant: 8.54858e-06   # N.s^2/rad^2
  moment_constant: 0.016         # m
  max_rotor_speed: 1000          # rad/s
  gravity: 9.81
  omega_to_pwm_coefficient: {x_2: 0.001142, x_1: 0.2273, x_0: 914.2}
  PWM_MIN: 1075
  PWM_MAX: 1950
  SIM_GZ_EC_MAX: 1000    # rad/s
  SIM_GZ_EC_MIN: 150     # rad/s
```

## Topic map

| Direction | Topic | Message type |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| in | `/fmu/out/vehicle_odometry` | `VehicleOdometry` |
| in | `/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1` | `VehicleStatus` |
| out | `/fmu/in/offboard_control_mode` | `OffboardControlMode` |
| out | `/fmu/in/vehicle_command` | `VehicleCommand` |
| out | `/fmu/in/vehicle_attitude_setpoint` | `VehicleAttitudeSetpoint` |
| out | `/fmu/in/vehicle_thrust_setpoint` | `VehicleThrustSetpoint` |
| out | `/fmu/in/vehicle_torque_setpoint` | `VehicleTorqueSetpoint` |
| out | `/fmu/in/actuator_motors` | `ActuatorMotors` |

Note the versioned topic name for `VehicleStatus` — see
[version mismatch](../setup/workspace-setup.qmd#versioned-topic-names).

---

## Switching modes at runtime

The control mode can be changed without restarting the node:

```bash
ros2 param set /offboard_controller control_mode 2   # -> thrust + torque
ros2 param set /offboard_controller control_mode 3   # -> direct actuator
ros2 param set /offboard_controller control_mode 1   # -> attitude (default)
```

The `OffboardControlMode` heartbeat automatically switches its active field
on the next publish cycle.
